title: Next Patient

lines.text: Monday OPD. Fever for three days. Body ache. Runny nose.

fact_notes: Lines 1-6: a typical OPD scene, not a real patient. The prescription slip is drawn in code and labelled RECREATION. Line 2 is Hinglish on purpose; use an Indian English voice, or record it with a real person.

Lines 7-10: NCDC multicentre point prevalence survey, 20 NAC-NET sites in 15 states and 2 UTs, WHO Global PPS method, 9,652 patients. 6,944 (71.9%) on antibiotics; 54.8% of them for prophylaxis (surgical 37.3%, medical 17.5%); 91% of surgical prophylaxis patients received it for more than one day. Reported 2024 (Down To Earth; Rajya Sabha PQ 263, 6 Feb 2024). Data likely collected around 2021-22, so no year is spoken.
Line 10 'one dose is usually enough': WHO and ICMR surgical prophylaxis guidance is a single pre-incision dose, extended no more than 24 hours.

Lines 12-13: ICMR AMRSN annual report 2023, as reported by Down To Earth: imipenem susceptibility of Klebsiella pneumoniae fell from 58.5% (2017) to 35.6% (2023); E. coli fell from 81.4% to 62.7%. The data come from tertiary-care hospitals, not the community. Check the exact numbers against the ICMR PDF before the final render.
Line 15: colistin is the usual reserve drug for carbapenem-resistant Gram-negatives in Indian ICUs; colistin resistance is also reported in AMRSN data.
Line 17: three illustrated, typical high-risk groups (neonatal sepsis, post-operative infection, ventilator-associated pneumonia), not real individuals.

Line 24: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare 'Red Line' campaign: antibiotic packs carry a red vertical line meaning prescription-only. Schedule H1 (Drugs Rules, 1945; in force since 1 March 2014) covers third- and fourth-generation cephalosporins, carbapenems and others.
Line 25: World AMR Awareness Week 2026, 18-24 November; theme 'One Health, one action: Prevent AMR now' (WHO).
